{"class": "fixable",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "page reads through the asynchronous I/O layer (orders table B-tree)", "component": "asynchronous I/O layer", "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "A full scan to sum(qty*price_cents) must read every orders leaf page, and every page read passes through the frozen I/O layer.",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 4394, "unit": "pages", "per_unit_cost_us": 1.0,
                                "total_ms": 4.4, "calling_context": "warm OS page cache, each page read once, assumed ~1 us per read"},
                 "max_cores": 1}],
 "floor_ms": 4.4, "L_delta": -3.33,
 "rationale": "The frozen floor (~4.4 ms of I/O-layer page reads) is far below T_R_upper, so no architectural certificate exists. Plans match, and almost all of Turso's cost is in mutable VDBE code: Statement::_step dispatch (~21%) and repeated op_column_range_fetch (~23%). Caching the parsed record header across column fetches and tightening the step/dispatch loop would cut well over the ~10–20 ms needed. A leaner shell start-up would save ~4 ms more."}
